from: the Rev D slim tag (BaggageClaims_Tag_RevD_Engineering.md and _Design.md in Files)
about: The Rev D slim leather-look tag the owner approved on 22 Nov 2026 at 19:00 ("yes this is perfect, a perfect design"): direction A Heritage, colourway A1 Saddle, one CR2032 with a 1 F supercapacitor, an nRF52832 on a custom board. The 2 x AA design's parts and wires are retired only while they still read as seeded; requirements and tests tied to two AA cells are brought to Rev D's figures, each an estimate where it is one. Every row names the Rev D document and section it comes from.

rows.sourceLocation: section 1, what you are choosing; section 4, direction A
rows.title: Which enclosure design ships?
rows.body: Rev D, the slim leather-look tag, offered in three directions and two colourways each, every one 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm with the same inside and passing the same 20 of 20 checks of its own generator. Chosen: direction A, Heritage (square shoulders cut at 45 degrees, saddle stitching in the thread colour, a blind-stamped oval maker's mark, a perforated panel across the top), colourway A1, Saddle: Bambu Lab PETG HF Peanut Brown body, Bambu Lab PETG HF Cream thread and lettering, Bambu Lab TPU for AMS Black strap. Renders, the assembly and the two print plates are in Files, folder Design and build.

rows.title: Which form factor ships?
rows.body: A slim leather-look luggage tag, 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm, about 62 to 64 g with the tracker (estimate), hanging about 10 mm under the handle on a TPU strap, with a pocket for an AirTag-style tracker behind a bayonet door and a name card in the back. It replaces the 80 x 60 x 42 mm box and the 2 x AA design (Rev B, and Rev C's box): about a third of the box's volume and 30 % of its thickness. The tracker's 8.0 mm sets the thickness.

options.label: 80 x 60 x 42 mm box on two AA cells (Rev B, Rev C)
options.outcome: About 80 dB at 1 m and about 6 months on a pair of cells; a large object dangling from the handle.

options.label: Slim tag, 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm, on one CR2032 (Rev D)
options.outcome: About 70 dB at 1 m and about 9 months on a cell (estimates); a custom circuit board replaces the breakout boards.

data.source: Rev D engineering, sections 0 and 5; Rev D design, section 2

rows.ruling: Owner, 22 Nov 2026, in his direction for Rev D: "more like a leather-looking, high-quality baggage tag ... change the double-A batteries to a watch battery to make it smaller ... We cannot have a large dangling object. It must have a pocket to fit an AirTag and be a little larger"; and at 19:00, of the Rev D tag: "yes this is perfect, a perfect design".

rows.title: Which lines go on the tag?
rows.body: As rendered and approved with the design: on the front, BAGGAGE CLAIMS / MK1 in the stamp and the tagline "Your luggage finally talks back." (the launch video script's line under the title card, 0:06); on the tracker door in the back, "FRAGILE — and emotionally unstable." (the owner's line, word for word). Lettering Montserrat Bold, an open-licence placeholder until a brand kit exists. No third-party name or logo anywhere.

options.outcome: As on the Rev D renders.

rows.title: Which cell powers the tag?
rows.body: One CR2032 lithium coin cell with a 1 F, 2.7 V supercapacitor that carries the speaker's bursts: the cell never drives the speaker; it refills the capacitor at up to 2.6 mA through 470 ohm, inside its 3 mA continuous rating, and the capacitor gives the 1 W peaks through a boost converter. 0.07 g of lithium metal, under the 0.3 g under which a device may stay on in checked baggage. No port, no charger; the user changes one CR2032 about every nine months (estimate).

options.label: Two AA alkaline cells, 3.3 V boost (Rev B)
options.outcome: Not lithium; needs a 2 x 46 mm battery bay and the 20 mm deep speaker: the box.

options.label: One CR2032 straight to the amplifier
options.outcome: About 53 dB at 1 m: inaudible in a terminal.

options.label: One CR2032 and a 1 F supercapacitor buffer
options.outcome: About 70 dB at 1 m, about 9 months (estimates); 0.07 g lithium.

options.label: One CR2450 and the same buffer
options.outcome: About 26 months, about 0.19 g lithium (estimate); the 24.5 mm cell does not fit beside the speaker without a wider tag.

options.label: LIR2450 rechargeable and USB-C
options.outcome: 0.43 Wh; a charging port in the face, a charger and a protection chip, and no louder.

options.label: Flat 150 mAh LiPo and USB-C
options.outcome: 0.56 Wh; a pouch cell in a bag that is thrown and crushed.

data.note: The airline rules, as read on 22 Nov 2026 (Rev D engineering, section 1). IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, 66th edition, Table 2.3.A (https://www.iata.org/contentassets/6fea26dd84d24b26a7a1fd5788561d6e/dgr-66-en-2.3.a.pdf): baggage with installed lithium batteries may go as checked baggage only if the batteries "contain no more than 0.3 g lithium metal or for lithium ion must not exceed 2.7 Wh"; portable electronic devices: "Devices in checked baggage must be completely switched off and must be protected from damage". IATA Guidance Document for Passengers Travelling with Lithium Batteries 2026 (https://www.iata.org/contentassets/6fea26dd84d24b26a7a1fd5788561d6e/passengers_travelling_with_lithium_batteries.pdf): in checked baggage "the device must be completely switched off (not in sleep or hibernation mode)", with a footnote exempting devices of 0.3 g or less of lithium metal, or 2.7 Wh or less. FAA PackSafe, Baggage Equipped with Lithium Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/baggage-with-lithium-batteries): "lithium content not exceeding 0.3 grams" or "a Watt-hour rating not exceeding 2.7 Wh"; "If you choose to equip a checked bag with a baggage tracking device, then it must meet the size limits above"; "Check with the airline before traveling with these devices". FAA PackSafe, Portable Electronic Devices Containing Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/portable-electronic-devices-with-batteries): devices in checked bags "must be completely powered off and protected to prevent unintentional activation or damage"; spare lithium batteries "are always prohibited in checked baggage". FAA PackSafe, Lithium Batteries (https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/lithium-batteries): lithium metal "limited to 2 grams of lithium content per battery". The CR2032's 0.07 g: the Duracell CR2032 sheet (https://www.duracell.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/CR2032CH_225mAh.pdf). The IATA documents were read through a web reader. Still to watch: airlines may set stricter rules, and no rule names a device that talks.

rows.title: Custom circuit board, 24 x 35 mm
rows.body: Two layers, 0.8 mm FR-4, ENIG (pads for the cell springs), corners R 1.5. It carries everything but the speaker, the supercapacitor and the tracker: U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, Q1, Q2, R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, C1, C2, PAS, Y1, L1, L3, S1, S2, BT1, and the programming pads J1 (a Tag-Connect TC2030 footprint, no part fitted). Components on the back side up to 1.2 mm high, the two cell springs on the front side, both switches on its right-hand edge. Clamped between four printed posts and four pads on the back plate. Price per board of a 5-board prototype order; it needs a design and a layout first (about $20 for the first five plus a stencil, estimate). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

geometry.basisSource: 24 x 35 x 0.8 mm: the Rev D design (engineering, section 4)

data.mountingHolesBasis: Placed for the app's generator, clear of the side switches: the Rev D note clamps the board on four printed posts but gives no positions.

rows.title: Board assembly
rows.body: Stencil and reflow by hand at one to five boards (own labour not costed, so $0), turnkey assembly at a hundred. 0.4 mm-pitch parts: not perfboard work. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

data.source: Own bench; an assembly house at 100

rows.title: Controller chip, nRF52832
rows.body: nRF52832-QFAA, QFN-48 6 x 6 mm, run from the cell directly; its radio is never started and no antenna is fitted. 512 kB flash of its own; the clips are in U3. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Crystals Y1 and Y2, 32 MHz and 32.768 kHz
rows.body: 2016 and 2012 packages, for U1. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: DC/DC inductors L1 and L2, 10 uH and 15 nH
rows.body: For U1's own DC/DC converter. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Motion sensor chip, LSM6DSO class
rows.body: 6-axis accelerometer and gyro, LGA-14 2.5 x 3 x 0.83 mm, +/-16 g and +/-2000 degrees a second, FIFO and wake-up interrupt, on SPI. Replaces the Adafruit MPU-6050 breakout, which is a third of the tag's inside and draws more than a coin cell gives with its gyro on. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Clip flash, 8 MB SPI NOR
rows.body: MX25R6435F class, wide supply: about 245 s of 16 kHz PCM or about 980 s as 4-bit ADPCM (calculated). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Amplifier chip, MAX98357A
rows.body: The I2S class-D amplifier of the 2 x AA design as a chip (TQFN-16 3 x 3) on the board; fed from the boosted 3.3 V only while a clip plays. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Boost converter, 3.3 V, TPS61023 class
rows.body: Starts from 0.5 V, switch of 3 A or more (recalled), 3.3 V out; raises the supercapacitor for the amplifier and is enabled only for a clip. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Boost inductor, 1 uH 3 A
rows.body: 2520 package, for U5. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Reverse-cell P-MOSFET
rows.body: SOT-23, in the cell's lead after the off switch, gate to ground: a cell fitted the wrong way does no harm. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Charge switch P-MOSFET
rows.body: SOT-23, switched by the controller (CHG_EN): it lets the cell refill the supercapacitor through R1 and stops at 2.6 V. Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Charge resistor, 470 ohm
rows.body: From the charge switch to the supercapacitor: 2.6 mA at 1.8 V on the capacitor, 0.85 mA at 2.6 V (calculated), inside the CR2032's 3 mA continuous. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Capacitor sense resistor, upper
rows.body: Divider from the supercapacitor to the controller's ADC (V_SC). Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Capacitor sense resistor, lower
rows.body: Lower half of the V_SC divider, to ground. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Cell sense resistor, upper
rows.body: Divider from the cell rail to the controller's ADC (V_CELL), read under the 2 mA charge load so a tired cell shows. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Cell sense resistor, lower
rows.body: Lower half of the V_CELL divider, to ground. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Boost enable pull-down
rows.body: Holds the boost converter off while the controller is unpowered or asleep, so a charged capacitor cannot drive the amplifier with the off switch off. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Cell rail capacitor, 100 uF
rows.body: Carries the controller's bursts (about 10 mA for milliseconds) off the cell. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Cell rail capacitor, 10 uF
rows.body: Beside C1 at the controller. Price: a share of the passives line (estimate).

rows.title: Other passives
rows.body: Decoupling and the DC/DC parts, about eight: the rest of the Rev D note's passives line ($0.80, $0.80 and $0.20 in all with R1 to R6, C1 and C2). Prices at 1, 5 and 100 units are estimates (Rev D engineering, section 2.6), not quotes.

rows.title: Supercapacitor 1 F, 2.7 V

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.2, the buffer; section 2.4, current budget
rows.setBody: One CR2032 lithium coin cell (the owner's "watch battery", 22 Nov 2026) with a 1 F, 2.7 V supercapacitor that carries the speaker's bursts. The cell runs the controller, the motion sensor and the flash directly (2.0 to 3.2 V) and refills the capacitor through 470 ohm at up to 2.6 mA, inside its 3 mA continuous rating; a boost converter, enabled only for a clip, raises the capacitor to 3.3 V for the amplifier. Asleep: about 12.5 uA at the cell (22.5 uA while the capacitor is kept full, the first 2 h after motion); awake about 0.74 mA. These are estimates from recalled data-sheet figures, not measured. The 2 x AA design (two AA cells and a 3.3 V boost for everything, about 0.25 mA asleep) is superseded.

setData.response: Sleep with the RAM kept; wake on the motion sensor's interrupt or the button

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.4, current budget and battery life
rows.setBody: Estimate, for the 2 x AA design's travel day (3 h awake, six clips of 3 s, 21 h asleep): about 3.0 mAh a travel day and 0.30 mAh a day at home switched on. With 180 mAh usable from a CR2032 down to 2.0 V, allowing for cold (225 mAh nominal on the maker's sheet): about 9 months at four travel days a month, about 6 at eight, about 20 switched on and never moved, and about 4 if the carousel keeps it awake 8 h more each travel day. The cell's self-discharge is not counted. The motion sensor's awake current is three quarters of the budget; keeping the gyro off until the accelerometer sees handling would take the four-day figure over a year (estimate). The 2 x AA design's figure was about 6 months.

No more than 85 dBA at 1 m, "to stay a novelty, not a nuisance" (the documents). Rev D: about 70 dB at 1 m at full level (67 to 73), 65 dB one step down: calculated from the speaker maker's 76.5 dBA at 3 W and 1 m, less 1.5 dB for a small sealed box and a perforated skin (estimate), with 1 W peaks into 4 ohm. That is 10 dB quieter than the 2 x AA design's 80 dB, about half as loud to the ear: a clear voice at arm's length (about 79 dB at 0.35 m) and at the carousel, not across a busy hall. The loss is the 28 mm speaker, not the cell. Not measured.

rows.title: Clips from the capacitor buffer
rows.body: The speaker's bursts come from the supercapacitor, so loud clips are rationed by its refill. From a full capacitor (2.6 V) about 2.5 full-level clips play back to back (two or three); after that one full-level clip every about 154 s, or one 5 dB down every about 49 s; empty to full takes about 8.5 minutes. Before a clip the firmware reads the capacitor: under 2.2 V it plays 5 dB down, at 1.9 V or under it skips the clip and logs it as busy. All figures are calculated (0.69 J a clip: 1 W peaks, 6 to 1 peak to average, 3 s, 72 % through the boost and the amplifier), not measured.

data.trigger: A gag allowed by the governor
data.response: Play at full level, 5 dB down under 2.2 V, or skip at 1.9 V

match.title: Off switch is a true disconnect

rows.setBody: The owner's ruling of 22 Nov: a physical OFF switch, in case the airport asks. Rev D: a side-actuated slide switch on the board's right-hand edge, its lever 0.5 mm under the edge surface in a slot so a knock cannot move it, in the cell's lead before everything: off, the cell is disconnected and the tag is completely switched off in the sense of IATA's portable-device row and FAA PackSafe. The supercapacitor keeps its charge, but nothing can draw it: the boost converter's enable comes from the unpowered controller and has a pull-down. With 0.07 g of lithium the tag may stay on in the hold; the switch is for when it is asked to be off.

rows.sourceLocation: section 3, firmware item 6; section 2.2, refill time
rows.setBody: The cell is read through a switched divider under the 2 mA charge load, so a tired cell shows. Thresholds about 2.7, 2.5 and 2.3 V (estimates, to be set on the bench), in place of the 2 x AA design's 2.4, 2.2 and 2.0 V: below the first clips are quieter, below the second the low-battery line plays once, below the third no clips, sleep only. The capacitor is read before each clip (Clips from the capacitor buffer). The brown-out counter of the 2 x AA design goes.

setData.trigger: Cell under about 2.7 / 2.5 / 2.3 V under load

rows.setBody: A coin cell fitted the wrong way must do no harm: the P-channel MOSFET Q1 in the cell's lead blocks it. No brown-out is expected: the controller runs from the cell and the audio from the supercapacitor, and 100 uF and 10 uF on the cell rail carry the controller's bursts. The capacitor-voltage gate replaces the 2 x AA design's brown-out count.

setData.response: No damage; works when the cell is put in the right way

rows.setBody: An LSM6DSO-class sensor on the board at 104 samples a second (not 100: the windows counted in samples scale by 1.04, or the driver resamples), +/-16 g and +/-2000 degrees a second, read in batches from its FIFO on a watermark interrupt (INT2). Asleep: the accelerometer alone in low-power mode at 12.5 Hz with its wake-up interrupt (INT1). The axes are set again for the board's orientation (the board flat in the tag, +Y toward the strap). The owner's MPU-6050 stays the reference for the bench prototype; the detection rules take g and degrees a second and do not depend on the chip. The gyro's zero offset is learnt at rest and never from a steady turn.

The tag on a suitcase handle must still work after the case is dropped 1.0 m onto concrete, six times, one on each face (an estimate of rough handling; the documents say shocks to 40 g survival). Rev D: rim 3.0 mm all round, outside corners R 4 or more, a 1.6 mm front skin and a 2.4 mm back plate that sits inside the body's rim (a knock on the edge reaches the body, not the joint) on eight snap hooks; the tracker, the cell and the capacitor held through their own centres; the board clamped between posts and pads; both doors bayonets bearing on a lip; nothing hinged; the strap TPU. Not tested.

Rev D, direction A Heritage, colourway A1 Saddle: a slim tag, 62 x 92 x 12.8 mm, PETG in two colours with a TPU strap, a strap slot, the perforated speaker panel, a tracker pocket behind a bayonet door and a name-card pocket in the back. The motion sensor is on the board, which is clamped rigidly between printed posts and pads, never foam mounted. The 80 x 60 x 42 mm box is superseded.

rows.appendBody: Rev D: the motion sensor is soldered on the custom board, and the board is clamped between four printed posts and four pads on the back plate; the breakout and its screws are gone.

rows.sourceLocation: section 2.5, clip storage; section 3, firmware item 5
rows.appendBody: Rev D: the clips are in an 8 MB SPI flash (U3) as 16 kHz PCM (about 245 s) or 4-bit IMA-ADPCM (about 980 s), decoded by the controller and sent over I2S at 16 kHz; the boost converter and the amplifier are enabled only for the clip.
Rev D has no USB port: a pack goes in as a flash image through the programming pads at the maker, or through a later variant with USB (nRF52840). The USB-drive idea is not possible on Rev D.
Rev D has no USB-C: firmware and clips go in through SWD pads (a Tag-Connect TC2030 footprint). Where the debug log comes out on Rev D is not yet decided.
Rev D: the nRF52832's radio is never started and no antenna is fitted.
Rev D: this sketch is for the XIAO ESP32S3, which Rev D does not have; it needs the changes in "Firmware changes for Rev D" before it can build for the nRF52832 board. Not proved for Rev D.

rows.title: Lithium within the checked-baggage limit
rows.body: The tag's own lithium is at most 0.3 g of lithium metal (or 2.7 Wh of lithium ion), so it may stay on in checked baggage: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations, 66th edition, Table 2.3.A, and FAA PackSafe, Baggage Equipped with Lithium Batteries (both read 22 Nov 2026). Rev D's CR2032 holds 0.07 g (Duracell's sheet). A CR2477 (about 0.31 g, estimate) would be over. The tracker in the pocket is its own device with its own cell. FAA PackSafe also says to check with the airline; airlines may set stricter rules.

rows.title: Firmware changes for Rev D
rows.body: The firmware for the 2 x AA design (BaggageClaims_MK1_RevB.ino with bc_detect.h and bc_detect.cpp) is not rewritten; Rev D needs these changes to it (Rev D engineering, section 3): (1) Board and core: the nRF52832 (Arduino nRF5 or Adafruit nRF52 core, or Zephyr), not the ESP32 core. Preferences becomes the nRF's own flash store; LittleFS goes on the external SPI flash. (2) Pins: a new pin map on the custom board, fixed with the layout: SPI to the motion sensor and to the flash (a bus each on the schematic), the sensor's INT1 (wake-up) and INT2 (FIFO mark), I2S (SCK, LRCK, SDOUT) to the amplifier, AMP_SD, BOOST_EN, CHG_EN, two ADC inputs (V_CELL, V_SC), MODE, SWD. (3) Sensor driver: the MPU-6050 register code is replaced by the LSM6DSO class at 104 Hz, +/-16 g, +/-2000 degrees a second, FIFO with a watermark interrupt and a wake-up interrupt with its own threshold units; new scale factors; the up axis set again for the board. (4) Sleep: System ON idle with the clock and a pin sense on INT1 (no deep-sleep restart; state stays in RAM); the two-hour dark wake is a clock compare. Optional: gyro off until the accelerometer sees handling. (5) Audio path: read V_SC before a clip; at 1.9 V or under skip it (logged busy), under 2.2 V play 5 dB down; enable the boost, wait about 2 ms, enable the amplifier, stream from the flash through an ADPCM or PCM decoder to I2S at 16 kHz; then amplifier off, boost off, charging on until 2.6 V. The full level keeps peaks at 1 W into 4 ohm. (6) Battery policy: the cell thresholds (about 2.7, 2.5, 2.3 V under the 2 mA charge load, set on the bench) replace the AA thresholds; the brown-out counter goes and the capacitor gate replaces it. (7) Loading clips: through SWD at the maker as a flash image, or a later USB variant (nRF52840); no USB drive. (8) Unchanged: the event rules, the governor, the picker, the clip naming, the counts and the button meanings. None is made yet.

setData.pass: Rev D: meter in series with the cell, 2 h after the last motion (the capacitor no longer kept full): at or under 25 uA, against an estimate of about 12.5 uA. In the first 2 h the estimate is about 22.5 uA. The documents' 200 uA and the 2 x AA design's 0.25 mA are superseded.
Rev D: awake and being moved, no clip, the capacitor full: under 1.5 mA at the cell, averaged over 10 s (estimate about 0.74 mA). The 2 x AA design's 15 mA is superseded.
Rev D: with a CR2032 in and the switch on, the cell rail (VCELL) reads 2.0 to 3.2 V (a new cell about 3.0 V); switch off, 0 V. The supercapacitor charges to about 2.6 V and stops.
Rev D: the 3.3 V rail (3V3A) feeds the amplifier only: about 3.3 V while a clip plays, 0 V between clips with the boost converter off.
Rev D: switch off, meter in series with the cell on its most sensitive range: 0 uA (under the meter's resolution), the cell rail at 0 V, and no clip can play with the capacitor charged.

Rev D: loudest clip at full level with the capacitor full (2.6 V), sound level meter (A-weighted, fast) at 1 m on the perforated panel's axis: record the peak. Pass under 85 dBA; record it against the estimate of about 70 dB (67 to 73).

Rev D: on a bench supply in place of the cell, set the thresholds (about 2.7, 2.5 and 2.3 V under the 2 mA charge load, estimates): below the first clips are quieter, below the second the low-battery line plays once, below the third no clip plays; no reset loop from 3.2 V down to 1.8 V.
Rev D: a CR2032 fitted upside down in its cup for one minute, then correctly: no current over 1 mA while reversed, and the tag works afterwards.

Rev D: tag on a packed case, dropped 1.0 m onto concrete, once on each of six faces: the back plate stays on its hooks, both doors stay locked, nothing rattles, and it still passes the Drop and Weigh-in tests.
Rev D: with a CR2032 in and the switch on, no hot spot by touch after 30 s, and the controller answers on the programming pads (SWD).
Rev D: with the cell out, VCELL, V_SC and 3V3A each read open to ground; continuity on every net matches the schematic.

rows.appendBody: Rev D: this test is for the 2 x AA design's board. The nRF52832 build waits for the firmware changes (requirement "Firmware changes for Rev D").

data.pass: Rev D: from a full capacitor, play full-level clips back to back: two or three play (estimate 2.5), then the next plays 5 dB down or is skipped and logged busy; about 154 s later one full-level clip plays again (estimate). Log V_SC before each clip.
The fitted cell's own data sheet states 0.3 g of lithium metal or less (a CR2032: 0.07 g on Duracell's sheet), and no second lithium cell is fitted in the tag.

rows.because: The Rev D design gives the clips to the supercapacitor; the recharge test measures how many and how often, and the loudness test the level.
The lithium limit is met by the cell chosen; the test reads its data sheet.

rows.requirement: Off switch is a true disconnect
rows.because: Rev D's off switch is S1 in the cell's lead; R6 keeps the boost off with the controller unpowered.
Rev D's supply: the cell, its contacts, the reverse-cell MOSFET, the supercapacitor and the boost converter.
The level is set by the 28 mm speaker, the amplifier and the gasket that seals its chamber.
The printed body is the enclosure; its pocket is sized to the tracker.
The sensor is soldered to the board, which is clamped in the body.
The cell and the capacitor are read through these dividers.
Q1 blocks a reversed cell; C1 and C2 carry the controller's bursts.
The printed parts carry the drop.
The firmware has to be ported to the nRF52832 and the external flash before it builds.
